term: moved by itself (ὑφʼ αὑτοῦ κινεῖσθαι), Aristotle's self-mover
definition: A thing is moved by itself when, as an animal, the whole moves itself, one part being the mover and another the moved (Physics VIII.4, 254b27-33; VIII.5, 257b2-13). Lean: the primitive `SelfMovedIn`, which is not `MovesIn x x r` (DISAMB-SELF-MOTION).
